newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: TULIP SAYS COULD MAKE PROFIT IN FULL 1997.
newsitem.headline: TULIP SAYS COULD MAKE PROFIT IN FULL 1997.

text.p: PC maker Tulip said on Thursday continued turnover growth meant it might not book a loss over the full year 1997.
"Barring unforeseen circumstances, management therefore expects that the full 1997 year need not be closed with a negative result," Tulip said in a statement.
Tulip said earlier it narrowed its losses in the first half of this year to 6.78 million guilders from a year-earlier 12.75 million guilders.
It said it expected to book renewed year-on-year turnover growth in the second half of 1997. In the second half of 1996 it booked turnover of 262 million guilders.

"Due to the contribution of the new factory (improved efficiency) as well as turnover growth, the second half of the year will show an increase in profits relative to the same period in 1996," Tulip said. In the 1996 second half it posted a net profit of 2.7 million guilders.
Consequently management was assuming that the full year need not be closed at a loss, the personal computer maker said.
